The test `test_loc_with_non_string_categories` checks whether it is possible to use a non-string category in the CategoricalIndex for label-based indexing. However, this test fails with a TypeError indicating that the indexers passed (in this case an integer) cannot be used for label indexing on a CategoricalIndex.

Following the execution path of the failing test, we can see that the error occurs in the `CategoricalIndex._convert_scalar_indexer` method. This suggests that the issue lies in how the CategoricalIndex handles scalar indexing with non-string categories.

Upon further inspection of the code snippet for this method (retrieved using `get_code_snippet("pandas.core.indexes.category.CategoricalIndex._convert_scalar_indexer(key, kind)")`) we can see that it is expecting a label (a string) as the key for indexing. However, when trying to use an integer key with a CategoricalIndex having non-string categories, this expectation is not met.

The code attempts to convert the scalar indexer (`key`) into a label using `self._formatter_func(key)` in line 702 of `pandas/core/indexes/category.py`. This method assumes that the indexers are labels (strings) and tries to format them accordingly. However, if the category names are not strings, this formatting operation fails.

Consequently, un-formatted keys are being returned by the CategoricalIndex for scalar indexing operations with non-string categories, which leads to the TypeError demonstrated by the test.
